Terms of Service

B2B contract terms between Praxmate and clinics. Last updated: June 2026.

Note: These Terms apply to entrepreneurs within the meaning of § 14 BGB (German Civil Code). Patients (consumers) do not enter into a contract with Praxmate — they contract directly with the booking clinic.

§ 1 Scope

(1) These Terms of Service ("Terms") apply to all contracts between Hasi Elektronic — Owner: Hamdi Güncavdı (the "Provider" or "Praxmate") and customers (the "Clinic") regarding the use of the Praxmate SaaS platform.

(2) A customer within the meaning of these Terms is exclusively an entrepreneur within the meaning of § 14 BGB — in particular medical practices, dental practices, naturopaths, therapy practices, clinics and other healthcare facilities.

(3) Deviating, conflicting or supplementary terms and conditions of the Clinic shall only become part of the contract if the Provider expressly agrees to their validity in writing.

§ 2 Subject matter and scope of services

(1) Praxmate is a cloud-based software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution for managing patient appointments, waiting lists, practitioners, treatment types and patient communication.

(2) The scope of features results from the respective tariff description on praxmate.de.

(3) Praxmate provides the Clinic with the software for use via the internet. No installation on the Clinic's systems takes place.

(4) The Clinic's patients are not contractual partners of Praxmate. The treatment contract and any consumer relationships exist exclusively between patient and Clinic.

§ 3 Conclusion of contract and trial

(1) The presentation of plans on the website does not constitute a binding offer but an invitation to submit an offer.

(2) By registering and selecting a plan, the Clinic submits a binding offer. The contract is concluded upon confirmation by email or by provisioning of the platform.

(3) Praxmate grants a free trial of 7 days from registration. No fees apply during the trial. If the contract is not cancelled within the trial period, it converts seamlessly into a paid contract under the selected plan.

(4) The Clinic warrants that it is acting exclusively as an entrepreneur within the meaning of § 14 BGB.

§ 4 Plans and fees

(1) The following plans are available (monthly prices, exclusive of statutory VAT):

PlanPrice / monthTarget group
WaitlistEUR 9 netWaitlist only
SoloEUR 39 netSingle practice / 1 practitioner
TeamEUR 69 netMultiple practitioners
ClinicEUR 119 netClinic / multi-location

(2) Invoicing takes place monthly in advance via our payment processor Stripe Payments Europe Ltd., Ireland.

(3) Price changes will be communicated to the Clinic by email at least 6 weeks before the end of the month. In this case the Clinic has a special right of termination effective on the date of the price change.

(4) In the event of payment default, Praxmate is entitled to suspend access after prior reminder with reasonable notice.

§ 5 Obligations of the Clinic

(1) The Clinic undertakes to keep its access credentials secret and to protect them against unauthorized access. Optional 2FA (TOTP) is recommended.

(2) The Clinic is solely responsible for the lawfulness of the data it enters into Praxmate — in particular the data-protection lawfulness of patient data.

(3) Vis-à-vis its patients, the Clinic is the data controller within the meaning of Art. 4 (7) GDPR. Praxmate acts as processor in this respect (see § 9).

(4) The Clinic shall not misuse the platform, in particular not for sending unsolicited advertising, distributing unlawful content, or attacking Praxmate's systems.

§ 6 Availability and service level

(1) Praxmate targets an annual platform availability of 99.5 % on a yearly average, measured at the Cloudflare edge network.

(2) Planned maintenance will, where possible, be carried out outside common business hours and announced at least 48 hours in advance.

(3) Outages due to force majeure, internet backbone failures or sub-processors (e.g. Cloudflare outages) are outside Praxmate's sphere of influence.

(4) Daily encrypted backup in Cloudflare R2 with a retention period of 30 days. Data restores at the Clinic's request require written notice.

§ 7 Liability

(1) Praxmate is liable without limitation for intent and gross negligence, for injury to life, body or health, and under the Product Liability Act.

(2) For slight negligence, Praxmate is liable only for the breach of material contractual obligations (cardinal obligations) and limited to the typical foreseeable damages.

(3) Liability per case of damage is limited to the amount of net fees paid by the Clinic in the 12 months preceding the occurrence of the damage.

(4) Any further liability — in particular for lost profits, indirect damages, or data losses caused by the Clinic's misuse — is excluded.

(5) The Clinic is obliged to make its own data backups of the data it enters into Praxmate at regular intervals (at least weekly), insofar as the data is relevant to the Clinic.

§ 8 Term and termination

(1) The contract is concluded for an indefinite period.

(2) Either party may terminate the contract with a notice period of 14 days to the end of the month.

(3) Termination by the Clinic is made via the Stripe Customer Portal or by email to h.guencavdi@hasi-elektronic.de.

(4) The right to extraordinary termination for cause remains unaffected. Cause for Praxmate includes in particular repeated payment default, serious misuse, or breaches of § 5 of these Terms.

(5) After contract end, the Clinic's data will be deleted from the production systems within 90 days. Backups are rotated after 30 days as per § 6 (4). Before deletion, the Clinic can export its data via the GDPR export function.

§ 9 Data protection and processing

(1) Insofar as Praxmate processes personal data of patients on behalf of the Clinic, a data processing agreement (DPA) under Art. 28 GDPR is concluded between the parties. The DPA is provided to the Clinic upon registration and shall be deemed part of the contract.

(2) Details of the data processing — in particular the sub-processors (Cloudflare, Stripe, Resend) — are set out in the Privacy Policy.

(3) Transfers to third countries are based exclusively on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs).

§ 10 Final provisions

(1) The law of the Federal Republic of Germany applies, excluding the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods.

(2) The exclusive place of jurisdiction for all disputes arising from this contract is Vaihingen / Stuttgart, insofar as the Clinic is a merchant, legal person under public law, or a special fund under public law.

(3) Should individual provisions of these Terms be or become invalid, the validity of the remaining provisions shall remain unaffected.

(4) Changes to these Terms will be announced to the Clinic by email at least 6 weeks before the effective date. If the Clinic does not object within this period, the changes shall be deemed accepted. The right to object will be specifically pointed out in the notification.

(5) We do not participate in dispute resolution proceedings before a consumer arbitration board; this applies notwithstanding the fact that consumers are not contractual partners.
